reviews.text: Samson had the potential of being a pretty good noir action-adventure, but it’s currently a broken, repetitive grind. The good: - The overall vibe of the game, it really feels like a cool mix of original Mafia games with GTA IV and Max Payne - Pretty satisfying hand combat, feels nice and heavy - The driving model is a mixed bag, but I quite like it The bad: - TONS of bugs and glitches, sometimes even completely game-breaking. I couldn't proceed with the story further than mission 2 so I just had to replay grindy missions over and over again till I paid my debt (game's main goal) and... that's it. - Extremely repetitive content, missions seem fun at first, but they quickly get boring once you realize you're doing the same thing in the same places for the second or third time. - Collisions in this game are extremely bad and inconsistent. If you play for a while, you'll see what I mean. Get ready for gates you drive through tens of times suddenly not letting you through. - The upgrades system based on collectibles (188 boards to smash?!) is just lazy work.

[h1] Middle of The Road [/h1] I've had the chance to follow this game's development for a while and I'm happy the developers released this at the price point they did, instead of the usual high rise we've grown accustomed to. Overall, my first impressions are that I wish Steam had a mixed recommendation as there's some good and some bad with Samson. I like the open world, and I'm not expecting a 50+ hour journey for what I paid, it's clear that this game is a tight knit 10-20 hour experience and that's totally fine by me! The voice acting is really nice and I'm enjoying this aspect. I'm still getting used to the driving mechanics, so I will edit this further. The graphics are good for my rig, I haven't experienced any major FPS drops or crashes whilst playing. Although I'm sure future patches will be at the developers list. The combat to me lacks a bit of impact that a fun beat em up game should have! The lack of guns is fine if the hand to hand melee combat is a fun time but I'm still not too sure on this. I'd say at this point, the developers needed some extra time to put key parts together, however I'm enjoying what it is currently. I'd definitely say to get this on a sale, but I'm glad it's already at a much cheaper base price than people expected!

I was pleasantly surprised by the performance - no stutters on my setup, even though it’s built on the notoriously demanding UE5. For $25, it’s definitely a steal. Sure, there are some bugs and a lack of explanation for certain mechanics, but I’m pretty confident the devs will work hard to polish the experience.

追加评价：希望制作组能够优化开车手感，由于游戏内有不少追车或逃脱的任务，驾驶手感的不适应让我根本无法流畅完成任务，显得很狼狈，虽然还是能通过但是会觉得自己表现很差劲，感觉无论是战斗还是开车都应该向sleeping dogs看齐，作为同样注重近战且有非常多追车和逃离追击的开车任务的前辈，前辈的近战手段更多且开车手感非常优秀。 之前评价：从定价和没有中文就可以看出来制作组确实穷，而且steam页面里制作组发的文章也可以了解到制作组情况不佳，所以放弃了很多野心勃勃的东西转而把全部力量放在自己擅长的东西上做出了这样一个可以称得上是独立游戏的作品，我觉得这个价格完全可以接受甚至是实惠，玩了下感觉质感还可以的，起码人物建模和场景什么的看起来完全不是粗糙，光追看起来也不错。要知道，88元在中国一般都是2D的独立游戏的价格，何况samson是一款3D游戏。 但是玩了一会儿（因为要睡觉）后感觉bug和瑕疵肯定有，比如我在和一个路上随机的npc打架时，因为旁边有物体，结果他自己移动时穿模进入物体里了，当然不是整个身体，是腿的一部分，还有就是我感觉初始车辆的驾驶手感有些笨拙，再就是我感觉踢门这个功能居然不能踢到门后的敌人很让人遗憾，我甚至专门趁敌人来的时候关上门就为了试试我踢门能不能让门伤害他，但貌似踢门的功能更多是耍帅。 再就是打击感我觉得没有问题，战斗感觉手感良好，但仍然有不足，就是我觉得近战格斗的方式有点单一，我好像只能轻重攻击，格挡，闪避和开启无双模式？如果近战是本游戏的主要战斗方式的话，是不是应该有连招系统呢？我感觉最好的例子就是热血无赖，当然有可能是因为我只玩了二十分钟体验了第一个任务，所以可能我并不知道有没有比如连招的东西。 总体来说，我觉得这个价格，在我玩起来还不错的情况下，也没什么理由打差评，当然我觉得制作组需要考虑制作中文版本，中文玩家是最大的游戏群体，而且我前面也说了你这个定价在中国区完全是很不错的定价。 配置的话我是全拉满，开了dlss性能和帧生成，有80到90帧且很流畅，感觉是完全ok的优化，且性能和质量模式除了帧率变化外画质区别很小。 From the pricing and the absence of Chinese language support, it's clear that the development team is indeed in a financially tight spot. Additionally, articles posted by the team on their Steam page provide insight into their challenging circumstances. As a result, they had to abandon many ambitious ideas and instead focused all their efforts on what they excel at, creating what can be considered an independent game. I find this price completely acceptable, even a good deal. After playing a bit, the overall quality feels decent—at least the character modeling and environments don't look rough, and ray tracing looks nice too. Keep in mind that 88 yuan is typically the price for 2D indie games in China, and Samson is a 3D game. However, after playing for a while (as I needed to sleep), I noticed there are definitely bugs and flaws. For example, when fighting a random NPC on the road, due to nearby objects, part of his leg would clip through into them as he moved. Also, I felt the initial vehicle handling was a bit awkward. Another regret is that the door-kicking feature can't harm enemies behind the door. I even特意 closed the door when enemies approached just to test if kicking the door would hurt them, but it seems the door-kicking function is more for show than practicality. Regarding combat, I think the hit feedback is fine, and the battle feels good. However, there's a lack in the melee combat system. It seems a bit one-dimensional—I can only perform light/heavy attacks, block, dodge, and activate the 'Overdrive' mode. If melee is the primary combat method, shouldn't there be a combo system? The best example I can think of is 'Sleep No More.' Of course, this might be because I only played for twenty minutes and experienced the first mission, so I might not be aware of combo systems if they exist. Overall, given that I had a decent experience and considering the price, I don't have much reason to give a bad review. That said, I believe the development team should consider creating a Chinese version, as Chinese players are the largest gaming demographic. As I mentioned earlier, this pricing is very reasonable for the Chinese market. In terms of configuration, I maxed out all settings and enabled DLSS Performance and Frame Generation. I achieved 80-90 FPS with smooth gameplay, indicating excellent optimization. The difference in visuals between Performance and Quality modes is minimal, aside from frame rate variations. Additional Review: I hope the development team can optimize the driving feel. Since there are many chase or escape missions in the game, the poor driving feel makes it impossible for me to complete the tasks smoothly, leaving me feeling quite embarrassed. Although I can still pass, I feel like my performance is very poor. It seems that both combat and driving should take inspiration from Sleeping Dogs. As a predecessor that also emphasizes close combat and has numerous chase and evasion driving missions, Sleeping Dogs offers more close-combat options and an excellent driving feel.

TL:DR; This is a game of small scope that tries to focus on melee combat and driving, sidelining pretty much everyting else. Melee combat and driving are the worst parts of this game. The animation breaks and input delay are insane. The game has sprinting melee attacks: you are guaranteed to miss every one of those, as the game requires you to be standing still to register that you are, in fact, fighting. The game has multiple vehicle missions where you need to ram enemy cars. 50% of the time, you take collisionnn damage, while they do not (despite T-boning them at high speed). The game has parry and dodge mechanics. If you dodge twice in a row near an enemy, your character does a mandatory full 360 degree turn while the game tries to calculate which way you should be facing. You are vulnerable while you do it. For a game that puts driving and fisticuffs at the front to have driving and fighting be the worst parts of it is downright shameful.

目前来看，作为一款售88元的游戏，内容仍然显得粗糙，入手需谨慎 黑暗粗粝的场景是该游戏的巨大亮点之一。在虚幻5加持下，Tyndalston肮脏颓废的街道显得极为真实可信，加上街道上来来往往的美国老车，让人仿佛置身《好家伙》的世界。这也是吸引我第一时间购买游戏的因素。 可惜的是，游戏的内容无法与如此吸引人的背景相匹配。游戏主打徒手格斗和追车，但是这两种核心玩法都显得欠缺打磨。格斗的打击感相对比较优秀，但是操作比较僵硬，且由于敌人时常穿模，闪避、格挡的反馈欠佳。追车时车辆的沉重感体现的较好，但是处于中心位置的“车斗”反馈不足，仅仅是通过反复的撞击把敌方车辆逼停而已。预告片中展现的敌方车辆腾空翻滚的场面比较难以复刻。 真正劝退我的是一个跟踪的任务。这个任务中，主角需要跟踪某人到罪犯老巢，但被跟踪对象警戒条的涨与落毫无逻辑可循，再加上被跟踪对象走得极为缓慢、甚至会像出bug一样一顿一顿地蹭着走，极度消耗玩家耐心。 由于这两种核心玩法的粗糙，Samson目前还不足以成为独树一帜的作品、而仅仅是“没有枪的GTA”。话虽如此，只要能够改进格斗与追车的手感，Samson仍有成为佳作的潜力。

I have been waiting on Samson since it's reveal way back in December 2025. It honestly looked amazing from what we got shown. An open-world action-adventure game with hand-to-hand combat. A game that has consequences and an unforgiving urban environment that pushes back... it sounded so damn good. To top that off, Samson was developed by the co-founder of Avalanche Studios and the Just Cause games, so I decided to grab the game because the developers sounded so passionate about this project with what they were saying. It had to turn out good... right? Well... I will get to all of that below so let's get to it shall we! [h1][b] What is wrong/Cons [/b][/h1] ⚫Why does the melee combat feel so... poorly done? Is it just me or is the melee combat arcade-like, for lack of better words. When the game got teased and developers got their interviews e.t.c one said ""Seriously, No Guns" for our character. Meaning, they are heavily emphasising some sort of in-depth brutal/bloody melee combat. So what went wrong? Saying "guns will make it to easy" and then making a sloppy melee system shows you have no experience. ⚫I was doing a contract, right. Walked into the building, picked up a frozen fish, went to melee some dudes and punched him into the wall. He was still alive. So, I went to punch him again. This failed me instantly. Dropped me out of the world and I had to restart my game. WHAT?!?!! ⚫During combat, you cannot zoom your camera out meaning a group or an enemy can easily sneak up on you and hit you for free giving them an advantage over you. Even if it's just you and 2 other guys, if you loose track of the other guy... he's probably about to "HULK SMASH" you into the floor. ⚫Another note about combat - why do I need to swing my fists before I can target my enemy? What I am saying is that there's no "LOCK ON" feature at all. Once you take care of the guy your fighting your character just drops out of fight mode completely ruining the immersion. ⚫AND ANOTHER note about combat - why do enemies sometimes just stand there and not try to throw a punch at me? It's a MELEE focused game. Do I always need to throw the first punch for them to INSTANTLY dodge my attack and then hit me? I've noticed when you stop attacking, they attack you... like... fully drop out of the melee stance you do. This is a game breaker for me. ⚫Driving around feels... slippy/slidey. You might think to yourself "it's just his car". No. Get into another car. It's the same. Not only that... I've noticed that the cars are the same speed? Maybe I'm just not noticing the speed difference but... they feel the same speed. ⚫Drive near civilians and watch them goof out. One time, I was driving on the road and civilians started crossing... I slammed my brakes and all of a sudden they T-posed, hit my car and then randomly became a different set of civilians!?!?! WHAT?!?! Then another time I was doing a contract, got close to a guy near a van and he starting phasing through it, slowly rising above the van to then instantly drop to the floor like a sack of potatoes... then get back up and fist fight my car... what is this, AI GENERATION?!? serious question. ⚫I noticed during "cop chases", no matter where you go, no matter how far you go... they all seem to know your EXACT position at all times. How? Why? I drove miles away during a chase and watched my map... about 5 or so corners before you got to me... the police car took every single turn to my EXACT position. Even GTA 3 had better cop AI than this. It made them feel real. ⚫I have this "blurry" issue and "lighting" issue with the game. It's unbearably bright in some locations or when I go outside my apartment to begin the day and then as time goes on, the game gets this blurry black-ish filter over it. I don't know why but it's getting on my nerves. I think it's UE5 because every game I play that's UE5 has this issue at some point (until patch's and optimisation comes out). ⚫A funny one to end on - Why does it look like Samson has "sh*t" himself when he runs? I guess what I am trying to say is the animations are a tad... stupidly goofy. I personally do not believe a human worked on these animations. ⚫They have taken the time to add in over 200 collectables. I think there are over 400. Split between POI's, skill books, billboards to smash and 1 other collectable. Someone made a valid point about this is my comment section and I have to agree - it feels like they added these just to "pad out the game and waste your time". [h1][b] What I liked/Pros [/b][/h1] ⚫I like the map. It's really detailed and you can tell it's urban. [h1][b] An Online Article [/b][/h1] I read an article online about Samson after the game came out. Due to the game releasing in MIXED reviews on Steam - the creative director Christopher Sundberg said "this game will grow over time on all fronts; quality, gameplay and content". He promised improvements on gameplay and the technical side of things. I want to make this ABAUNDANTLY clear. We are NOT your "test subjects". You either optimise the game and test it fully before release or you damage the game's name, your studios name and all the developers jobs releasing a game in this state. I hate to say it but I am so SICK and tired of "RELEASE NOW, PATCH LATER" when it comes to UE5 games. [h1][b] My Verdict/TL;DR [/b][/h1] Just because it's got "good developers" behind it doesn't mean it will be a good game. I hate to say it... I really do but releasing a game in this state only puts your studio at risk and THEN you released a statement saying you promise "technical fix's" and "content" clearly shows a lack of polish and refinement. Did you test this at all before release? Did you make some things using AI? These are questions we shouldn't be thinking or asking. I miss the days when we knew a games released in a good, playable and enjoyable state. Now we have to wait for these "PROMISED" improvements. Samson is clearly FAR from finished. Samson is clearly lacking basic optimisation and bug testing. I cannot recommend a game in this state. Just to be clear - I am going to keep tweaking my PC settings, Nvidia settings and so on in hopes that I can fix.... whatever I can... [h1][b] 3.5/10. Another UE5 game that's un-finished, un-optimised buggy mess. Another UE5 "RELEASE NOW, PATCH LATER" game that will probably lead to another studios closure. [/b][/h1]

This is a pretty decent game, people just like to complain a lot. Here's a list of pros and cons and why or who I can recommend this game to. Reasoning: Aight, this is a quirky, glitchy game, it has janky animations, heavy vehicle handling and a repetitive story with quite an obvious constraint budget wise and it shows with the cut scene animations mainly. Voice acting is really good. You WILL enjoy this game if you either love grunge settings of the past century, brawling, and dont mind a roguelite playstyle where you level up day by day, rinse and repeat a few quests of your choice and dont mind exploring the extreme eye-candy trashy city of Tyndalston to pick up a few collectibles to level yourself up further. Pretty good soundtrack too. Pros: - Gorgeous graphics perfectly fitting for the city and performance that I think is really good for unreal engine, you will get stutters when driving with my hardware but they are not major or annoying. The game runs at a silky smooth fps on foot at all times of day. This is at 3440x1440 res. Almost all settings maxed. - Extremely well made map even if small in size, there are so many little areas that the game obviously encourages you to get out and explore rather thaan drive everywhere. There is huge detail placed into this city feeling like someone's falling apart hometown, the map is really a strong point for the game with suited audio work. - The game plays similar to Mafia 3, Mad Max and similarly to a 2010s open world game, a pro for me. - Open world freedom, you aren't constrained to the story and can do things at your own pace, find stashes to steal from dealers, run from the cops, explore, then just continue the story as you wish. - The price, that is just so rare these days and the developers humbly knew the quality of their game, unlike many majorly overpriced AAA games that release in a worse state. - Patches, the game is getting and did get a patch, with a road map in progress. Already had game breaking stuff fixed within the first week. Now, the cons: - Repetitive, yeah im not gonna put tons of hours into this for sure, but for the price and the fact ill probably play for 20-30 hours, thats more than ive put in a lot of larger more expensive titles, if i get bored of the game's playstyle, ill just play something else til i feel like coming back to this, but in these 14 hours at time of review, ive enjoyed myself. - Vehicles, theres like, 5 or 6 models and they're reused or customized for variety, i guess that shows the minimal budget. They drive okay, damage is okay, you can't steal occupied cars but that may be a story design choice, there are plenty of parked ones, and you can call your car at any time provided it isnt damaged. [strike] Damage is consistent though even on parked cars you steal, which im not too keen on, since the city is slowly littered with more cars i cant use. [/strike] <- patched - Animation jank, it shows a lot when you try to parkour over something, beating people has been semi fixed, but is getting more work, it isnt game breaking but, sometimes you may punch someone real hard up the ass thats having a smoke and they dont react until they drop the cigarette. - Lack of fight variety, for a game based on brawling quite heavily, you get maybe 3 different enemy types, but i really would have liked to see them have more move variety, and perhaps you being able to unlock more moves yourself. You can also press G and throw someone onto an object, the game doesnt tell you this directly. - Map size, it is small, while its a pro cause its so heavily detailed, it is also a con because you can get through it all quite fast, at least when not going into the small alleys. - Cutscenes, the game has a decent story of trying to get out of debt to save your sister, in a city completely against you, but without proper cutscenes and animations, and mission variety, its hard to get invested, it feels a little like an RPG where its more dialogue focused than anything else. My personal take away on this game, its worth the 25 bucks if you aren't a picky little b*stard, want a casual game to pick up and not need to spend time learning the mechanics too heavily, and enjoy grungy city settings and story. I could see the reviews rise to a "mostly popular - very popular" rank after a few patches, its not a perfect game, but its better than what some people say.

Samson is the kind of game that’s surprisingly hard to talk about — though not nearly as hard to play. The game suffers from a wide range of issues. Some of them might be fixable over time, but others feel deeply rooted in its core design — the kind of problems patches simply can’t solve. The most glaring flaw lies in its sense of purpose and storytelling. The narrative is presented in the most basic, surface-level way, lacking any real depth or emotional weight. It fails to create a meaningful connection with the player, and its dialogue is filled with clichés that quickly become tiresome. From beginning to end, there’s no truly memorable or impactful character, and the central premise — the protagonist’s sister’s debt — never evolves in a way that meaningfully affects either the character or the world around them. Nothing changes, nothing grows, and the world remains static throughout. Beyond the story, the mission structure — especially those tied to repaying debt — becomes a major problem. While story missions show occasional variety, the debt-related tasks are painfully repetitive. There are only a handful of mission types, and they start to feel stale very quickly. What might feel engaging for the first couple of hours soon turns into a chore, especially once you’ve repeated the same objectives multiple times. This frustration is amplified by the game’s roguelike mechanics. Losing all your progress and money upon death makes the experience far more punishing than it needs to be. Combined with the game’s chaotic and often unfair systems — like the erratic behavior of NPC drivers who can randomly run you over — it creates a loop that feels more exhausting than challenging. Time and again, your efforts are wiped out in ways that feel less like failure and more like bad design. There are, to be fair, a few redeeming qualities. The city itself looks visually appealing, the sound design — particularly the vehicles — is solid, and the combat system is serviceable. But these positives are overshadowed by issues like lifeless environments, repetitive NPCs, and a general lack of polish across the experience. At its best, Samson is a 3/10 game.

Samson, I'd love to give it a thumbs up and my recommendation, but I can't. The game devs really botched the whole experience with the time issue. Samson is a small open-world game based around driving and running small gigs for the local mobsters. Kinda like a mix of GTA 2 and Driver games, straight from the late '90s, made with the modern Unreal engine. The protagonist is a tough guy who has seen and done his share of nasty things, and now has to do even more, to pay his debts and save his sister and the neighborhood from even nastier people than himself. A solid B-movie plot, so to say. The playground is the port town of Tyndalston. It's very small, in comparison to most open-world games that you ever played. However, the artwork, the level of detail of every alley and backstreet of the slums that all used for the environmental storytelling, and actual gameplay, are really getting under your skin, in the first hours of gameplay. The usual open-world activities such as the search for collectables, and radiant set of renewable everyday tasks, are quite okay, as a basic concept. However, you gotta take into account that the whole game consists only of driving and fighting missions, with occasional running around. And while driving feels interesting, the fighting part is bad on the conceptual level. The devs tried to fix it in every patch, but it's like trying to make a butterfly out of an earthworm. Kinda fruitless effort. And yet, even with that stupid and incoherent melee combat system, which makes half of the missions quite dull, the game as the whole could be a fun experience. See, the artwork and a feeling of immersion in the surroundings, in that vibe of living in the '90s somewhere in the God-forbidden slums, is really a 10/10 hit to the nostalgia, at least for some of us (even for those who never lived in the slums or/and in the '90s). The issue that ruins the game is the time management. You see, the main story line can be finished in 2-3 hours of gameplay. The search for collectables, and all of the stuff basically needed so you can say that 'you've seen all that the game has to offer' - can be done in 12, maybe 15 hours. But! In order to 'complete' this game, you'll need much, much more, and that'll be a totally disastrous gaming experience, where you'll be playing the very same missions over and over, then intentionally losing missions again and again, then skipping days after days, without doing anything or progressing anyhow... Only to complete those stupid achievements, such as 'Payback' and 'Car Care'. Samson brings us to arguably the worst place in the world, somewhere in the absolute urban desolation of either upstate New York or Midwest America. I honestly do not know which is more horrifying, but what we do get out of Samson is a lot of really good ideas and one of the best urban environments in a game yet. I cannot praise the visual fidelity of the city enough, it really does feel like the absolute worst parts of urban America, which in many ways, are more dangerous than much of Fallujah, Iraq during the peak of the war. There is a lot to say about Samson, I think some of it is good? The music is sparing, but genuinely very good all things considered. It being a rarity is an odd case. The impact of the fighting, while the fighting itself is beyond poor, is extremely satisfying. And while everything has a very B-tier 90s movie vibe, there is something charming about the soulful take on the genre. More developers should focus on winding things back as far as big open world goes for more intimate urban experiences. Ultimately, the game feels like the worst two missions from the beginning of GTA IV, with the entire map being Hove Beach, combined with a half baked mechanic from Mafia 2. The very same mechanic that, if you paid the debt off before it was due, actually was a game breaking bug that prevented you from beating the game. In tribute to this game breaking bug, Samson is a full fledged remake of that very same bug, they even were so faithful as to make it impossible to actually beat the main story. Scripts do not work, animations are generally of a lower end that do not match the AAA visuals. Its a single A game with barely an AA budget and for some reason, AAA graphics. Optimization is poor, as to be expected with an Unreal indie game with the default graphics menu. The story was remarkably grounded, but the gameplay certain feels too gamey to fully embrace the tone and "thesis" of what the developers were going for. The potential here is great, however. While comparing it to its contemporaries is a bit inappropriate, I do think its fair to compare it to say, the original True Crime games. That being said, the True Crime games were overly ambitious and full of bugs (and yes, gamebreaking bugs at that) but they were pretty functional overall. And the grandson of True Crime, Sleeping Dogs, is arguably better than the games it was inspired by. Samson... is certainly a game. It is the most game of all time. It is Samson. There is nothing like Samson. Samson as a character is kind of cool, pretty cool even. He is some mix between Rorschach from Watchmen and Haze from Anonymous Agony, with the aesthetics of Billy Ray Cyrus or the guy who plays the english voice for Mr Krabs. Combine this with his Mad Max boomer ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ car and you have a great concept. This isn't a review damning the entire game, rather, it is just saying "its still in the oven and it still may be undercooked when its over, but right now, at this moment, its bloody raw." Samson, probably, will gain some unironic praise when it pulls itself out of its development poverty. As of now, its clear that the developers are over worked and doing their best to salvage the game, as if they have 100k in debts to pay off themselves.

I hope we see liquid swords tackle another game like this as I'm always hungry for another beat 'em up/driving game like Mad Max, Sleeping Dogs, and Arkham Knight and from what I've seen here they are working with real talent.

Samson is an open-world action game that wears its scars proudly. Developed and published by Liquid Swords, the title drops players into the unforgiving streets of Tyndalston, a city that seems determined to consume anyone who calls it home. The story centers on Samson, a man returning to his troubled hometown with a single objective: save his sister while staying one step ahead of debt collectors, criminals, and the law. The premise is simple, but the game uses it effectively to establish a constant sense of pressure that carries through nearly every aspect of the experience. What immediately stands out is the atmosphere. Tyndalston is not a glamorous playground filled with endless activities. Instead, it is a grim and oppressive environment defined by deteriorating buildings, narrow alleyways, and a feeling that every corner hides another problem. The game's day-to-day structure reinforces this mood through mechanics that require players to meet debt payments while managing their limited actions. Every decision matters, whether it involves taking on dangerous jobs, exploring the city for opportunities, or avoiding unwanted attention. This approach gives Samson a unique identity among open-world games, favoring tension and resource management over freedom without consequence. Gameplay revolves around a combination of melee combat, exploration, and high-speed vehicular encounters. Samson relies primarily on his fists and whatever the environment provides, creating encounters that feel raw and personal. The combat system includes parries, counters, and a collection of upgrades that gradually expand the player's options. While the mechanics can occasionally feel rough around the edges, there is satisfaction in mastering the timing of a well-executed counterattack or turning a desperate fight into a narrow victory. Vehicles are more than transportation, serving as tools for escape, pursuit, and destruction during some of the game's more memorable sequences. The progression system complements the narrative by allowing players to develop Samson according to their preferred style. More than two dozen upgrades provide meaningful improvements, rewarding those who invest time into exploring the city's hidden opportunities. The dynamic police response system also adds another layer of unpredictability, ensuring that reckless actions have lasting consequences. These interconnected systems work together to make Tyndalston feel alive, even if the world itself occasionally lacks the density and interactivity expected from larger productions. However, Samson's ambitions are not always matched by its execution. Performance inconsistencies, technical hiccups, and occasional bugs can interrupt the experience. Some missions become repetitive over time, and the open world does not always deliver on the promise suggested by its premise. It is evident that Liquid Swords aimed high with the project, sometimes stretching beyond what its resources could comfortably support. Even so, the game's commitment to its vision remains admirable. Rather than feeling generic, Samson consistently offers something distinct, and that originality helps compensate for many of its shortcomings. Post-launch support has also played an important role in shaping the game's current state. Numerous updates have improved stability, adjusted combat balance, and addressed player concerns. The developer's willingness to continue refining the experience demonstrates a level of dedication that deserves recognition. While Samson may not have launched in ideal condition, it has steadily evolved into a stronger and more enjoyable game through continued attention and community feedback. In the end, Samson is an imperfect but compelling action title that succeeds through atmosphere, tension, and a memorable central premise. Its blend of urban survival, brawler mechanics, and consequence-driven gameplay gives it a personality that separates it from many of its peers. Players willing to accept a few rough edges will discover a game with genuine ambition and a world that remains engaging long after its opening hours. It may not redefine the genre, but it leaves a lasting impression and proves that a strong vision can often be just as important as technical perfection. Rating: 7/10

Review but also FEEDBACK/ REQUEST FOR DEVS PLEASE READ. Review: Overall it’s a really good game, if you grew up playing games like Driver, The Gateway and True Crime, this feels similar to those games in both good and bad, so let get to it. Good: - Atmosphere and presentation is really good (I love it a lot) - Some of the soundtrack is really good (there’s specifically a lofi sounding one that I love) - Mission structure is somewhat simple, but feels like an old era PS2/3 game which I like and gives it more charm - Story isn’t the greatest, but it’s good enough to carry the motive and doesn’t get in the way of the gameplay - Tons of missions, side content/stories that slowly develop as you play, as well as random encounters. This is something I wasn’t expecting as I went in blind but I liked a lot. - it’s challenging (I’m playing on the hardest difficulty) but sometimes extremely clunky and unfair (I’ll expand on this further down) - Combat can and is fun sometimes, but if you don’t learn and get properly acquainted fast, you’ll get frustrated very fast because it’s not the most polished, but I still like the challenge nonetheless. - Being pursued by cops/gangs is fun but simple, I like how I can hide in a parking spot, turn off the engine and have them drive around trying to find me, feels a lot like Watch_Dogs. Bad: - Driving isn’t entirely bad, but it’s more on the bad side and it comes down to how the handling feels in most terrains. It somewhat slippery and high on the input latency side. I don’t want 100% snappy arcade, but a bit more grip would be nice. - Car combat is extremely limiting, for example, the best and honestly only way to actually do damage is to use the side swipe attack while next to the enemy car, because if you try to ram them head on, either from the back, front or Tbone them, it ends up doing very little damage and in some cases annoyingly it does more damage to your car than theirs. - Hand combat can be great, but needs some work as my experience has been extremely spammy on their end, inconsistent on who am I attacking and who I can attack, not being able to run towards someone (kinda like an MMO when you’re in combat and you can’t sprint but rather stuck in a “in combat” speed), not being able to leave combat and run away and last but not least the damage received by enemies can range from a couple hits, to 2 slaps and I’m knocked out (at least on the hardest difficulty) - Map is relatively small so you end up seeing everything quite fast. My first pursuit mission ended up with me chasing them down the same path which ran circles around the map. FOR THE DEVS, PLEASE READ: These are things that you can either add as an update (and should to build up the game) or for a potential sequel (which I 100% believe this deserves one) - Swimming: the fact I can fall into the water and instantly die as if I’m Tommy Vercetti in GTA VC is annoying, can’t you add a basic swimming system from Unreal Engine, add colliders to the north side or around areas you don’t want us to access and a button to “warp to shore” similar to how Saints Row does it - Combat: I believe making it so where your analog stick is facing is where he should punch would fix a lot of the jank in the fighting, a lot of times I parry someone swinging behind me, but I can’t turn my stick to him and attack him specifically, it’s whoever is in-front of me and that sucks a lot. Also, idk if this is because I played on the hardest difficulty, but as soon as I parry one guy, immediately the second guy wants to attack, I parry him and the first guy immediately swings back, I have no room to breathe and get a combo in most of the time. - Radio station(s) would go a long way at adding more personality and liveliness to the world, a talk show perhaps, or the news. - Climbing: I love that I can climb a lot of places that normally I didn’t think I could and idk if that by design, because you guys didn’t think to block off every nook and cranny but keep it that way, if anything LETS US EXPLORE MORE. My feedback here is 3 things. 1) the camera always increases the FOV when I climb and it’s very dumb and distracting, just don’t change it the FOV. 2) when I’m climbing a box to get on top of something that’s above it, if I spam the jump button, it’s as if the game thinks I’m still on the ground floor and it repeats the first climb animation, idk how but that needs to be fixed. 3) lastly, when I jump while moving or running forward, he jumps 90% UP and 10% FORWARD, it feels very clunky and not intuitive, I want to leap forward so I can cross a rooftop easier. Mission length: I beat all the chapters and only after doing so is when I started the get missions with multiple objectives, I don’t know if it’ll continue to be that way, but I believe this is how it should be going forward, I want missions where I have to do multiple things in multiple areas around the map so that the stakes are high and the fear of getting knocked out and losing are even higher, but the reward is massive if completed. Final thoughts: I honestly think this game can easily turn into a franchise, either by sequels with Samson, or with another entirely new character that also has a debt to pay, but having their own entirely unique story with plot twist, investigations, heartbreaking moments and so on, either set in the same city (kinda like GTA episodes of liberty city), or a new city entirely. I don’t know how successful this game has been, but I truly hope the developers lean into it and give us more of this kind of games in the future . **Samson: A Tyndalston Story** is a short, gritty, and surprisingly tense open-world action game that wears its scars on its sleeve. Developed and published by Liquid Swords, it released on PC in April 2026 (with console versions planned later) and sits in that rare space of ambitious indie that almost pulls off something special. ### The Setup You play as Samson McCray, a hardened fighter who returns to the decaying city of Tyndalston after time away. He owes a dangerous underground syndicate a serious amount of money, and they’re holding his sister as leverage. Every day the debt grows. Every day you have a quota to meet. Miss it, and collectors start hunting you. Fail three days in a row and it’s game over. That simple pressure system is the best thing about *Samson*. It turns the usual open-world checklist into something with actual stakes. ### Combat and Gameplay Combat is pure close-quarters brawling. Light and heavy attacks, parries, environmental weapons, and momentum-based fights in tight alleys and backrooms. It’s intentionally raw and scrappy rather than flashy. When it clicks, it has a satisfying, brutal weight that fits the character. When it doesn’t, it can feel stiff and repetitive. Driving is the other half of the equation. Cars are blunt instruments. Ramming, drifting, and turning chases into destructive scrapes is often more fun than the fistfights. The skill tree (over 25 upgrades) lets you lean into either side — becoming a better brawler, a better driver, or a mix of both. The world itself is small but dense. Tyndalston feels lived-in and ugly in the best way: grimy streets, industrial wastelands, and a strong 90s crime-noir atmosphere. It doesn’t try to be a massive GTA clone. It’s more of a focused, street-level story with side activities and jobs that feed into the debt system. ### Presentation and Length The game looks good for its budget. The city has character, the lighting is moody, and the overall aesthetic sells the “broken man in a broken place” vibe. Story-wise, it goes to some dark, unexpected places involving gangs, drugs, and worse. It’s not reinventing crime fiction, but it has more bite than most games in this space. Expect around 8–12 hours for a full playthrough, which feels right for the $25 price point (often lower on sale). ### The Rough Edges This is where honesty matters. *Samson* launched in a rough state. Combat can feel janky. Some missions repeat too much. Technical issues and bugs were common at release, and the game doesn’t always feel as polished as its ambition. Steam reviews currently sit in Mixed territory for good reason. It has excellent bones, but the execution is uneven. That said, post-launch updates have helped, and the core fantasy still works if you meet the game on its own terms. ### Verdict *Samson* is not a polished AAA experience. It’s a scrappy, focused crime story with a clever daily-debt pressure system, strong atmosphere, and enough style to make the rough edges forgivable for many players. If you want a short, tense, street-level action game that doesn’t waste your time with endless padding, and you’re willing to accept some jank, it’s a solid buy — especially at its low price. It won’t convert everyone, but for the right player it hits a specific, satisfying note that bigger games often miss. **Score: 7/10** **Best for:** Players who like gritty crime stories, brawler combat, and games that create real pressure without being overly long.
